name: Chen Jiancheng
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2023); Forbes annual (2016-2025); Hurun Global (2016-2026); Hurun China (2009-2026)
forbes_bio: Chen Jiancheng is group chairman of Wolong Group, a manufacturer of motors, generators and drive controls; the multinational company also has interests in renewable energy and related resources.
The group's subsidiaries include three public companies, Wolong Electric Drive Group, Wolong New Energy Group and Brook Crompton Holdings.
Chen's daughter Yanni is chairman and CEO of Wolong Holding Group; his son-in-law, Pang Xinyuan, chairs Wolong Electric Drive Group and Brook Crompton.

name: Elisabeth Douglas
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2024-2025); Hurun Global (2026)
forbes_bio: Elisabeth Douglas is the widow of industrialist Gustaf Douglas, who died in 2023.
Born von Essen, both she and her husband came from nobility, but only she from wealth.
Gustaf Douglas was a Harvard graduate that ran state-owned TV channel SVT2 and newspaper Dagens Nyheter.
In 1985, Gustaf Douglas acquired a controlling stake in a struggling Swedish security firm, eventually turning it into investment firm Investment AB Latour.
The Douglas family still control Investment AB Latour, which has a large stake in the world's biggest lock producer, Assa Abloy.
Elisabeth and her sons Carl and Eric are all billionaires.

name: Zbigniew Juroszek
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2001-2025); Hurun Global (2022-2026)
forbes_bio: Zbigniew Juroszek is the founder of Atal S.A., a real estate developer listed in Warsaw, Poland.
Juroszek first founded Atal in 1990 as a supplier to clothing manufacturers, before investing in real estate.
He built his first residential projects in 2003; Atal now develops properties in Katowice, Warsaw, and other major Polish cities.
He now runs his business with his son Mateusz, who is the CEO of gambling company STS.
STS, which is owned by the father and son duo, provides betting services to over 1 million customers in Europe.

name: Huang Wen Tsai
forbes_bio: Huang Wen Tsai chairs Star River Group, a luxury residential property developer in China.
Star River employs some 10,000 workers.
Huang founded a lumber company, the predecessor of Star River, in Guangzhou in 1995.

name: Wang Zhenghua
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2022); Forbes annual (2015-2025); Hurun Global (2016-2026); Hurun China (2008-2026)
forbes_bio: Wang Zhenghua is a director and the largest individual shareholder of Spring Airlines of China, one of the world's largest budget carriers.
Wang was a district government official in Shanghai before he set up his first company, Shanghai Spring Tour, in 1981.
Spring has a fleet of 122 aircraft, according to the company's website.

name: Gao Yi
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2022); Forbes annual (2020-2025); Hurun Global (2020-2026); Hurun China (2015-2026)
forbes_bio: Gao Yi is the chairman of Yifeng Pharmacy Chain, which has more than 4,000 stores across China.
Yifeng employs more than 40,000.
Yifeng, headquartered in the central China city of Changsha, was founded by Gao in 2001.

name: Jörg-Uwe Goldbeck
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2025); Hurun Global (2026)
forbes_bio: Jörg-Uwe Goldbeck is co-CEO of the eponymous construction company, which his father, Ortwin Goldbeck, started in 1969 with just seven employees.
One of Germany's largest builders, Goldbeck's projects include factories, warehouses, schools, offices, parking lots and residential properties.
With more than 100 locations worldwide, the builder employs 12,500 people and manages more than 500 projects annually.
Goldbeck was one of the main developers for the Telsa factory in Germany.
He and his brothers, Jan-Hendrik (co-CEO) and Jörg-Uwe, each own about a third of the company.

name: Rao Wei
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2021-2025); Hurun Global (2021-2026); Hurun China (2020-2026)
forbes_bio: Rao Wei chairs Shenzhen New Industries Biomedical Engineering, a supplier of clinical laboratory instruments.
In 1997, at age 33 year, Rao joined New Industries Biomedical Engineering when it was a trading company with only a dozen people.
Shenzhen New Industries went public on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in 2020, raising $192 million; the funds will be used for R&D and manufacturing.

name: Arthur Levine
forbes_bio: Arthur Levine cofounded the buyout firm Levine Leichtman Capital Partners with his wife Lauren Leichtman in 1984, five years after the couple were married.
LLCP has managed $14.8 billion of institutional capital across 15 funds since inception, and currently manages $10.2 billion in assets.
The firm's target sectors include business services, franchising and multi-unit, education and training, and engineered products and manufacturing.
Successful exits have included Tropical Smoothie Cafe, Wetzel's Pretzels and Nothing Bundt Cakes.
Prior to entering private equity, Levine was president of Westwood One, a radio syndicate.
As a couple, Levine and Leichtman share a fortune worth an estimated $2.6 billion.
forbes_facts: In October 2024, Levine and Leichtman bought the National Women's Soccer League's San Diego Wave FC for $113 million.

name: Sarah Humphreys Atkins
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2025); Hurun Global (2026)
forbes_bio: Sarah Humphreys Atkins is an heiress to the Galena, Kansas-based Tamko roofing fortune.
Her grandfather E. L. Craig started the company in 1944 at the age of 69 in an old streetcar barn in Joplin, Missouri.
Today, Tamko is the fourth-largest manufacturer of roofing shingles in the United States. The company recorded $1.2 billion in 2023 revenue.
The Humphreys family sold a 25% stake in the business to the Carlyle Group, a $447 billion (assets under management) private equity firm, for an undisclosed sum in 2019.
Sarah and her brother David, and their respective families, split the remaining 75%.
Atkins is married to SEC commissioner Paul Atkins. Both she and Atkins are on Tamko's board of directors.
forbes_facts: Paul Atkins, who was nominated by Donald Trump, is serving his second stint as SEC commissioner; he previously served for six years under George W. Bush.
